The Hanau cells belong to the old Hesse-Kassel (Hanau page: inherited by the Landgrave in 1736).

Cliopatria then has no Electorate shape for 1806-1813, which is right: Napoleon 'occupied the country and expelled him' after Jena-Auerstedt in 1806 and 'in 1807, with the Treaties of Tilsit, the area was annexed to the Kingdom of Westphalia'. The Hanau lands, which Westphalia did not take, stayed under French occupation and from 1810 belonged to the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt (Hesse-Hanau page). ledger.note: 1803: William I of Hesse-Kassel is made Prince-elector. 'Raised to the dignity of Prince-elector (Kurfürst) William I' in 1803 (infobox 'Established 1803'); the Recess page: 'Baden, Hesse-Kassel, and Württemberg gained status by being made electorates' and the Recess 'became law on 27 April' (month from that page). The Electorate page gives only the year.

region.text: 'some former French territory around Mainz' / 'land around the former Electorate of Mainz', minus the Hanau lands

ledger.note: 1803: compensation around Mainz. William was 'compensated for these losses with some former French territory around Mainz' (the 1801 cession to France); the Landgraviate page: 'in 1803 it was compensated with land around the former Electorate of Mainz'. The pages name no town (the Recess page has no Hesse-Kassel row; the Electorate of Mainz page says only how the right bank went to Hesse-Darmstadt and the Nassau princes, and is silent on Hesse-Kassel), so the region is a placeholder: the part of Cliopatria's 1803 shape within 60 km of Mainz, now without the Hanau lands, which the Hanau page shows Hesse-Kassel had held since 1736 ('which included Hanau, were inherited by the Landgrave of Hesse-Kassel'). What is left is one cell (about 250 km2) near 8.45 E 50.17 N. The electorate-of-mainz dossier records no matching loss to Hesse-Kassel.

region.text: the Electorate except the Hanau lands: 'Napoleon occupied the country and expelled him'

ledger.note: 1806: France occupies Hesse-Kassel. William I 'signed a treaty of neutrality with Napoleon Bonaparte'; 'After the Battle of Jena-Auerstedt, Napoleon occupied the country and expelled him.' The page gives no month; the battle falls in autumn 1806 (the kingdom-of-prussia dossier dates it 14 October 1806). This event covers the land that Westphalia took in 1807; the Hanau lands are entered separately (next event) because Westphalia did not take them.

region.text: the Hanau lands, Hesse-Kassel's since 1736: the cells of Cliopatria's 1805 and 1820 shapes within 30 km of Hanau (3 + 7, 8 distinct)

ledger.note: 1806: the Hanau lands are occupied. Hesse-Hanau page: in 1806 the Holy Roman Empire was dissolved and Hesse-Cassel absorbed into the French satellite Kingdom of Westphalia; 'Hanau came under French military occupation, then in 1810 was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt'. The page gives no separate year for the occupation; 1806 is the year of the sentence before it, and the Westphalia page excludes Hanau from the kingdom (next event).

region.text: the Electorate except the Hanau lands

ledger.note: 1807: the occupation of this land becomes annexation. The Electorate page: 'In 1807, with the Treaties of Tilsit, the area was annexed to the Kingdom of Westphalia'; the month is the Westphalia page's date for the Treaty of Tilsit, 7 July 1807. The Hanau lands were not part of Westphalia and stay occupied until 1810 (Hesse-Hanau page).

region.text: 'the Electorate of Hesse-Cassel ... with Schaumburg, excluding Hanau, Schmalkalden and Catzenellnbogen'

ledger.note: 1807: Hesse-Kassel goes into the Kingdom of Westphalia. 'The Electorate of Hesse-Cassel was included, with Schaumburg, excluding Hanau, Schmalkalden and Catzenellnbogen'; Cassel became its capital. Only Hanau is cut out of the region (30 km circle, as in the Hanau events below): Cliopatria's 1805 shape has no cell at Schmalkalden (10.45 E 50.72 N) and the Katzenelnbogen lands are not placed by any page. Westphalia page: created at Tilsit, 7 July 1807; its Cliopatria row begins in 1809.

region.text: the Hanau lands, Hesse-Kassel's since 1736: the cells of Cliopatria's 1805 and 1820 shapes within 30 km of Hanau (3 + 7, 8 distinct)

ledger.note: 1810: the Hanau lands pass from French occupation to the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt. Hesse-Hanau page: 'Hanau came under French military occupation, then in 1810 was incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt'. The Grand Duchy of Frankfurt page confirms Hanau among the lands 'combined into the new Grand Duchy of Frankfurt' in 1810 after Dalberg lost Regensburg; neither page gives a month.

region.text: the Hanau lands, Hesse-Kassel's since 1736: the cells of Cliopatria's 1805 and 1820 shapes within 30 km of Hanau (3 + 7, 8 distinct)

ledger.note: 1810: Hanau is incorporated into the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt, a French satellite (Hesse-Hanau page; Grand Duchy of Frankfurt page: 'his remaining territories of Aschaffenburg, Wetzlar, Fulda, Hanau, and Frankfurt were combined into the new Grand Duchy of Frankfurt'). The Elector had been expelled since 1806, so this is a change of holder, not of the Elector's own rule. The grand duchy has no dossier yet (counterparts_needing_dossiers).

region.text: the Hanau lands, Hesse-Kassel's since 1736: the cells of Cliopatria's 1805 and 1820 shapes within 30 km of Hanau (3 + 7, 8 distinct)

ledger.note: 1813: Hesse-Cassel's sovereignty over Hanau is restored. Hesse-Hanau page: 'It was not until after the German War of Liberation in 1813 that the sovereignty of Hesse-Cassel was restored.' The same page says the incorporation of Hanau into Hesse-Cassel 'was not completed until the death of prince-elector William in 1821' and Cliopatria draws Hanau in the Electorate only from 1820; no page gives a month, so the event carries none (the Elector's own return to Kassel on 21 November 1813 follows). The Electorate page adds that the Elector was 'to receive back all his former territories, or their equivalent'. The Grand Duchy of Frankfurt page is silent on the return (it says only that the grand duchy ceased after December 1813).

21 November 1813: the Elector returns to Kassel. After the Battle of Leipzig 'the French were driven out ... on 21 November, the Elector returned in triumph to his capital, Kassel'; a coalition treaty followed on 2 December. The Westphalia page: Prussian troops occupied Westphalia on 26 October 1813 and it 'was then dissolved'. The year 1813 is implied by the page's context. Cliopatria's shape starts in 1814 and its Westphalia row runs to 1813. The Hanau lands are entered in the event above (Hesse-Hanau page); this event covers the Westphalian part.

region.text: Fulda ('the Congress of Vienna resurrected it as the Grand Duchy of Fulda and gave it to the Electorate of Hesse in 1815')

ledger.note: 1815: the Congress of Vienna gives Fulda to Hesse. 'the Congress of Vienna resurrected it as the Grand Duchy of Fulda and gave it to the Electorate of Hesse in 1815'; Fulda had been given to the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt in 1810, occupied by Austria from 1813 and by Prussia from 1815. The Prussian dossier records no matching loss.

region.text: what Cliopatria adds between its 1815 and 1820 shapes beyond Fulda and the Hanau lands: seven cells near Gelnhausen and Schluchtern (9.25-9.52 E, 50.15-50.38 N), the Werra border (9.9 E 50.93 N), Schmalkalden (10.27 E 50.84 N) and two on the Rhine-Main (8.22 and 8.45 E, 50.16 N)

ledger.note: c. 1820: the rest of the eastern and Rhine-Main lands. Cliopatria's shape grows from 10,530 to 13,815 km2 in 1820; Fulda (1815, Fulda page) and the Hanau lands (restored 1813, Hesse-Hanau page) explain most of the rise, and what remains is about seven cells (some 1,800 km2) that no page opened dates or names. Pages opened and silent on them: Electorate, Landgraviate, Hanau, County of Hanau, Schmalkalden, Grand Duchy of Frankfurt, Recess. The Electorate of Mainz page says only that the Congress of Vienna 'divided his territories between the Kingdom of Bavaria, the Electorate of Hesse-Kassel (or Hesse-Cassel)' (and the Grand Duchy of Hesse and Frankfurt) without naming lands: a lead for a gap-filler (the Final Act of Vienna). The date is Cliopatria's.
20 June 1866: Prussia occupies Kassel. The elector 'threw in his lot with Austria' and 'Kassel was occupied (20 June)'. The page names the capital only; a 40 km circle stands for the occupation.

1866: occupation becomes annexation. 'By the Peace of Prague, Hesse-Kassel was annexed to Prussia'; the month is that of the Peace of Prague, 23 August 1866, as the kingdom-of-prussia dossier dates it from the Austro-Prussian War page.

1866: Prussia annexes Hesse-Kassel. 'By the Peace of Prague, Hesse-Kassel was annexed to Prussia' (infobox 1866); the Province page: the province 'had already come into being through the annexations of Hesse-Kassel, Nassau, and Frankfurt in 1866'. The kingdom-of-prussia dossier carries the matching gain (23 August 1866).
1866: the Electorate of Hesse ceases. The infobox lists 1866 as the year of annexation by Prussia; the Province of Hesse-Nassau was formally formed by Royal Decree of 7 December 1868 (Province page).

certainty.note: No page opened gives boundary lines; the 1803 Mainz-area gain is unlocated and 1806-1813 the state held no land (Hanau was under French occupation to 1810, then in the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt, restored 1813).
Frontiers after the Congress of Vienna settlement are treaty lines, though no page opened lists them; the Hanau, Fulda and Schmalkalden edges and the western exclaves are less certain than the core.

notes: Cliopatria's seven shapes: 1803 and 1805 kept; there is no shape for 1806-1813 (right: the Electorate was occupied by France in 1806 and annexed to Westphalia in 1807, so it held no land); 1814 kept; 1815-1819 adjusted for Fulda; 1820 and 1840 kept unverified (page budget: five pages); 1866-1867 (330.6 km2) marked wrong because the whole Electorate was annexed in 1866. The end year is 1866 whereas Cliopatria's row runs to 1867. The Electorate page gives no area, so no ratio could be computed. The 1803 Mainz-area gain cannot be located from the pages and sits at confidence 2 with a placeholder region; the electorate-of-mainz dossier records no loss to Hesse-Kassel. The Hanau and other eastern lands that enter Cliopatria's shape in 1820 are recorded as one confidence-1 event with an unnamed counterpart; a gap-filler should open the Hanau page, the Congress of Vienna Final Act and the Hesse-Kassel pages for 1815-1820 (and Schmalkalden). The kingdom-of-prussia dossier lacks a loss for Fulda in 1815 and its Cliopatria row ends 1863. The counterpart for the 1807 loss is kingdom-of-westphalia, whose Cliopatria row begins only in 1809, leaving 1807-1808 without a Westphalia shape. The three war entries rest on the Electorate page alone: no war page was opened. REVIEW FIXES (2026-10-31): Hanau is no longer an unoccupied rump. The ledger now has Hanau under French occupation from 1806 (not annexed to Westphalia), its loss to the Grand Duchy of Frankfurt in 1810, and the return of Hesse-Cassel's sovereignty in 1813 (Hesse-Hanau page), with the 1814 and 1815 keyframes adjusted to include it; the page says the incorporation was completed only in 1821 and Cliopatria draws Hanau from 1820. The 1803 Mainz placeholder no longer takes in Hanau (Hesse-Kassel's since 1736). The 1820 gain is narrowed to the seven cells that remain unexplained. The Grand Duchy of Frankfurt has no dossier yet.
